title: Euripidis Hecuba, Orestes, Phoenissae (Barocci 120)
shelf_note: A glossed Byzantine manuscript of Euripides (Orestes 954–981 on this leaf), 14th c. It fits a classical/Greek manuscript shelf. No tradition or collection is set, so there is nothing more to check it against.
structure_note: The structure says pages_translated 0, but the book field says 217 and this page carries a translation, so the counters disagree (E2). There are 15 printed backsteps and 15 repeats over 120 'printed' numbers. That reads as manuscript foliation (or numerals the OCR guessed at) taken as page numbers, not as a broken sequence: this verso carries no number, only a '+' mark at the head. The facing recto shows as a strip at the right edge; the OCR rightly ignores it.

missing.english:
No one with oracles <gloss>upon</gloss>, nor the Pythian
Phoebus seated on the tripod
missing.why: Nothing tells the reader that this is the Messenger's closing line to Orestes, or that the Pythian Phoebus is Apollo of Delphi, whose oracle ordered the matricide. Without that the line means nothing.

missing.english: as one sunk into madness and laments
missing.why: The red speaker marks on the leaf (Chorus, then Electra) are dropped, so the reader cannot tell who speaks or where Electra's lament begins.

missing.english: from the earth-born race of Pelops
missing.why: A general reader needs to know that Pelops is the ancestor of Orestes' house (the Atreids), the house whose ruin the song mourns.

book_verdict: The leaf is Orestes 954–981 (the end of the Messenger's speech, the Chorus, and Electra's strophe and antistrophe). The OCR invents or garbles most body lines, drops one line, and breaks the Persephone line into fake glosses. The translation turns all of this into confident English with an invented 'Antistrophe' heading and LaTeX leaks. A Hellenist would flag it on sight.
